headline: The CBAM extension never names automotive, but reaches it seven times through the combined-metal-products category
body:
[DRAFT — TODO-GEORGE: connecting prose only; every number below is computed and gate-checked]

No provision in the CBAM extension names the automotive sector. Seven of the file's rows reach it anyway, and all seven arrive the same way: the proposal adds a 'Combined metal products' category to the CBAM goods annex, which pulls downstream steel- and aluminium-containing manufactured goods into the embedded-emissions regime — and with them the industries that assemble those goods.

The mechanics are technical: SCP-04 creates the category, and CALC-03 changes how the number is computed for it, deriving the precursor mass from the content of input goods in the finished product rather than from a direct measurement. Neither row reads like sectoral policy, and neither names an industry beyond steel and aluminium.

The exposure table says what that category is made of. Basic metals — steel and aluminium, which FIGARO carries under one code — supply 5.1% of the automotive sector's total inputs in the EU view, and vehicles take 9.5% of the basic-metals sector's output, its second-largest customer after fabricated metal products (17.8%).

TODO-GEORGE: one connecting sentence on what a precursor-mass rule does to a sector that is never named in the text imposing it.

evidence.notes: Counts are taken across every row in data/cbam.json: auto appears in no row's sectors_named and in seven rows' sectors_reached (SCP-04, SCP-06, CALC-03, CALC-06, CUST-04, GOV-03, CBAMB-SCP-07). SCP-04 and CALC-03 are cited as the category's creation and its calculation rule. The shares are the stored FIGARO figures under code C24, which the exposure file's own note flags as shared between steel and aluminium: C24 at 5.1% of auto suppliers, C29 (vehicles) at 9.5% of steel customers, C25 (fabricated metal products) at 17.8% — all EU view. basis_status is mixed because the cbam register file is read from both the adopted base regulation and the proposed extension.
